headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: Devin can write shared code and use MCP/network, while Botpress can ingest content and install packages, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no documented isolation or provenance controls, and Devin can use MCP plus broad networked integrations. A shared channel is not explicitly documented, so the pathway is inferred rather than proven. Because Devin can act autonomously inside its workspace, injected content from Botpress outputs could be treated as instructions if bridged through files or integrations.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into Devin-readable files or MCP messages
IF Devin parses Botpress-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any file or MCP bridge between the agents
Add provenance tags to all Botpress outputs
Require manual review before Devin executes Botpress-authored text
Restrict Devin MCP servers to allowlisted schemas only

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin explicitly reads cloud workspace files and repo clones and sends data through GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, and MCP integrations. Botpress has no documented data-class restrictions or egress controls beyond network_egress:none, so if shared files or tickets contain sensitive content, Devin can leak it through its outbound integrations. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default enterprise workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress writes sensitive content into a shared workspace or ticket
IF Devin forwards that content into Slack, Jira, Notion, GitHub, or an MCP server
mitigations: Keep sensitive Botpress artifacts out of shared workspaces
Remove write access to Slack/Jira/Notion for the Devin session
Use redaction before any handoff from Botpress to Devin
Limit Devin integrations to read-only where possible

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Devin can execute shells, install packages, modify git state, write filesystems, and run browsers with parallel sessions. Both agents therefore overlap on mutable code and workspace surfaces, and Devin's shared-state integrations increase collision risk. With no locking or coordination documented for the pair, concurrent writes can corrupt repos or overwrite each other's changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a lock file or PR-only workflow
Disable parallel sessions on the shared repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a long-running planner-executor that acts autonomously, so if it consumes Botpress output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes, tickets, or messages. Botpress can generate support content that Devin may treat as facts or instructions, and Devin has downstream action authority through GitHub, Slack, Jira, and Notion. The interaction is inferred, but the blast radius is broad and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Devin uses Botpress output as a source of truth without verification
IF Devin turns that output into commits, tickets, or outbound messages
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin acts on Botpress output
Add a verification step against source documents
Mark Botpress output as untrusted input in prompts
Restrict Devin from auto-posting to external systems

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source with no residency or retention details, while Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace that handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and writes to Slack, Jira, and Notion. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and data handling, but no specific regulated data class like PHI or EU PII is documented here. The uncertainty keeps this below high.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive customer data is placed into Devin-managed integrations
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between Botpress and Devin workflows
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Document retention for each integration
Disable unnecessary logging in Devin-connected tools
Route deletion requests through a single owner process
